headline: GOLD, SILVER CRATER: Metals Tumble as Hot April CPI Slams Door on Fed Rate Cuts, Silver Sheds 5.6%
snippet: Gold fell $77 to $4,489/oz (-1.70%) while silver shed 5.6% to $73.36/oz on May 19 as April CPI came in above forecasts, eliminating near-term Fed rate-cut expectations and lifting real yields. The gold-to-silver ratio widened to 61.2:1, with silver's industrial demand sensitivity amplifying the selloff even as physical premiums in Asia held constructive.

headline: SIGMA LITHIUM CRASHES 15%: Company Fights Brazil Court Ruling Over Mine Waste as Coordinated 'Fake News' Attack Hits Shares
snippet: Sigma Lithium (TSXV: SGML) filed a legal appeal on May 18 against a local Brazilian judge's ruling tied to waste-management allegations at its Grota do Cirilo operation, alleging a coordinated media campaign timed to coincide with a positive company announcement drove a 15% share collapse. The company said no payments are currently due, that the case could take years to resolve through Brazil's courts, and that a site visit by legal authorities confirmed environmental compliance.

headline: BALD HILL BACK: MinRes Restarts Australian Lithium Mine After 18-Month Shutdown as Spodumene Prices Recover
snippet: Mineral Resources announced May 19 that its 100%-owned Bald Hill mine in Western Australia will begin crushing and mining operations in June, targeting first spodumene concentrate production in July after being placed on care and maintenance in November 2024. At 165,000 dmt/year capacity, Bald Hill's return makes MinRes the only company globally operating three hard-rock lithium mines simultaneously, with first shipment from the Port of Esperance expected in FY2027 Q1.

headline: Royal Gold HALVES Hod Maden Equity Stake, Converts to 2.5% NSR Royalty to Slash Capital Exposure on Turkish Project
snippet: Royal Gold cut its direct equity interest in the Hod Maden JV from 30% to 15% on May 17, simultaneously securing a new effective 2.5% net smelter return royalty that preserves attributable production of approximately 9,000 GEOs/year without ongoing capital calls. SSR Mining also sold its 20% stake to Turkish partner Lidya Madençilik, which takes over as operator; deal expected to close H2 2026.

headline: EQUINOX ABSORBS ORLA: $18.5B All-Share Deal Creates North America's New Senior Gold Producer, Targets 1.9Moz Annually
snippet: Equinox Gold (TSX: EQX) and Orla Mining (TSX: OLA) signed a definitive at-market merger on May 13 valued at US$18.5B, with Orla shareholders receiving one Equinox share per share held. The combined company — anchored by the Greenstone, Valentine, and Musselwhite mines in Canada — has an immediate run-rate of 1.1 million oz/year and a fully funded pipeline to 1.9 million oz, instantly making it the second-largest Canadian gold producer.

headline: Meridian Mining Opens New Footwall Discovery at Álamo: Drill Hole Returns 3.5m @ 2.4g/t Au, 1km From Existing Infrastructure
snippet: Meridian Mining (TSX: MNO) reported discovery hole CD-852 at the Álamo target on May 14, returning 3.5m @ 2.4g/t Au, 0.5% Cu, 9.5g/t Ag, and 0.7% Zn at 108.9m depth within Brazil's Cabaçal VMS belt — the highest gold grade encountered in the Santa Helena footwall to date. The target sits on a 1.6km IP anomaly open along strike and up-dip, and lies just 1km from the Santa Helena Central infrastructure, raising the prospect of a second operational hub.

headline: First Mining Gold Confirms High-Grade Continuity at Quebec's Duparquet in 16,577m Drill Campaign, Multiple Zones Extended
snippet: First Mining Gold (TSX: FF) released final results from its 16,577m 2025 drill program at the Duparquet project in Quebec on May 19, confirming high-grade gold continuity across the North, South, and Minuit zones with multiple significant intercepts. Management described Duparquet as the company's strategic flagship, reinforced by the drilling's demonstration of consistent grade and geometry along key contact zones.

headline: LASSONDE TARGETS $17,250 GOLD: Legendary Mining Financier Says U.S. $40 Trillion Debt Is the 'Detonator' Mainstream Banks Are Missing
snippet: Pierre Lassonde, co-founder of Franco-Nevada and one of mining's most credible long-term investors, published a forecast in May 2026 targeting $17,250/oz gold, arguing the U.S. federal debt crossing $40 trillion is a structural fiscal detonator that institutional banks forecasting $5,000–$6,000 are still dramatically underweighting. Lassonde's call is the most bullish public forecast from a credentialed industry voice and stands in sharp contrast to ING's $5,000 year-end target and J.P. Morgan's $6,000 longer-term view.

headline: MP Materials Posts Record Quarter: 917 Metric Tons of NdPr Oxide in Q1, Revenue Up 49% as Mountain Pass Strategy Pays Off
snippet: MP Materials (NYSE: MP) reported record Q1 2026 NdPr oxide production of 917 metric tons (+63% YoY) at its Mountain Pass facility in California, with total revenue jumping 49% to $90.6M and Adjusted EBITDA swinging from a $(2.7)M loss to $36.6M. The company advanced its heavy rare earth separation circuit toward Q2 commissioning and accelerated construction of its 10X expansion project, moving the U.S. closer to full domestic rare earth processing independence.

headline: Silver Heads Into SIXTH Consecutive Year of Supply Deficit; 762 Million oz Drawn From Above-Ground Stocks Since 2021
snippet: Silver is entering its sixth consecutive year of physical supply deficit in 2026, with cumulative draws from above-ground stocks since 2021 now approaching 762 million ounces — roughly nine months of total global annual mine production. Supply cannot meaningfully respond to price signals since approximately 70% of silver is produced as a by-product of gold, copper, and zinc mining, making primary mine response to price rallies structurally limited.

headline: Chile's Cochilco Lifts 2026 Copper Price Forecast to $5.55/lb, Eyes $5.10/lb in 2027 on Electrification Demand
snippet: Chile's state copper commission Cochilco raised its average 2026 copper price forecast to $5.55/lb, citing firm global demand from electrification, EV adoption, and AI data center buildout — with J.P. Morgan alone estimating data center copper demand at 475,000 metric tons in 2026. Cochilco expects prices to remain elevated in 2027 at $5.10/lb as structural demand from the energy transition continues to outpace new mine supply.

headline: Argentina Clears 13 Mining Projects Under RIGI as Copper-Lithium Pipeline Nears $42 Billion in Committed Investment
snippet: Argentina's RIGI large-investment incentive framework has approved 13 mining projects with total committed capital exceeding $42 billion as of May 2026, with Economy Minister Luis Caputo confirming two additional approvals on May 14 totaling $2.1B. The pipeline is dominated by copper and lithium projects and positions Argentina as the most active new mining jurisdiction in the Americas, ahead of a multi-decade resource development cycle.
